label: D1: a1 side (upcoming or previous choice is a1)
explanation: Fires only at D1 (none at GO or D2), on about 41% of D1 steps, with the same rate at every window position. Within D1 it is selective for the a1 side: the upcoming GO choice is a1 (91.5% of mass) and/or the previous choice was a1. The policy logit choice > 0 does about as well (F1 0.76, mass recall 0.97). D1 with upcoming action a1 alone gives F1 0.77 and mass recall 0.92. Adding the previous choice a1 (an observed input) gives F1 0.78 and mass recall 0.96 on dev. The upcoming choice is marked FUTURE, but it is the agent own computed choice, which is allowed. Using only observed variables (prev_action == 1, falling back to the upcoming choice on the window first trial) scores about the same (F1 0.78). A model-based outcome rule (prev state S1 rewarded or S2 unrewarded) does worse (F1 0.57-0.67). Prev reward = 1 raises the rate (78% of mass), but the reward term does not add to the predicate. Mostly silent on D1 before an a2 choice following an a2 trial. Many a1 D1 steps are inactive (precision about 0.72), and the misses are mostly in the lowest activation quartile (only 42% of that quartile is covered). The weak activations come around switches, for example D1 right after an a2 trial that precedes a switch to a1. In the example windows magnitude is largest on the window first trial and drops over a run of a1 trials. Also, it is zero above a value of about 8.1, i.e. when the value head is high.
